capabilities.restrictions: Agent instructions are applied when creating the sandbox.

Cloud sandboxes write one workload profile in `/home/agent`. Mixins use the workload's profile and cannot specify a `directory`. Unsupported required profiles prevent creation; optional ones are skipped.
Docker Sandboxes does not use these session commands.
Accepted since v0.45.0, but Docker Sandboxes does not execute the declared session commands.
Requires a selected `agent-skills@1` destination. Bundled skills remain available with `--skills=off`.
Local sandboxes mount the shared skills store. From v0.48.0, discovery paths also receive bundled skills.
In cloud sandboxes, credentials scoped to installation remain available after setup.
Requires `user.name` and `user.email` in the host Git config.
Users can [select host directories](../use-kits.md#choose-directories-for-kit-host-mounts) at creation time. Cloud sandboxes reject required entries and skip optional ones.
Restricted to approved OCI builder kits. Local and Git kit sources do not receive registry access.
Local startup hooks run alongside the agent, rather than blocking its launch.
Keeps a local sandbox running after its last session disconnects.
Cloud sandboxes keep installation-phase network access after setup.
Cloud sandboxes enforce host rules, but not HTTP method or path restrictions. Installation-phase access remains after setup.
Cloud sandboxes expose IPv4 TCP ports only. See [Port address families](#port-address-families).
Accepted by the local runtime, which runs Docker-in-Docker containers in privileged mode inside the sandbox VM.
Workload CPU and memory defaults are applied. The `gpu` field does not select GPUs; cloud creation rejects a required GPU request.
Docker Sandboxes launches the agent using the workload command.
Requires SSH-agent forwarding to be enabled and a host SSH agent to be available.
Kit requests for USB device access are not supported.

Local sandboxes provide block storage or tmpfs and [retain block volumes across removal and recreation](../use-kits.md#keep-kit-data-when-recreating-a-sandbox). Cloud sandboxes use ordinary sandbox disk at the declared paths, including for tmpfs requests.
